text.content:
Everything in this class is tuned to one table. Read it at session zero, and make sure the table reads it too, because it is the thing most likely to cause a disagreement later.

Sky stateThe Saint isMultiplierFrequency
Normal day~15% weaker than a comparable martial×0.85~11 days in 13
Ascendant — their sign rises~30% stronger×1.301 day in 13 (7.69%)
Zenith — their sign rises Exalted~100% stronger×2.001 day in 260 (0.385%)

Two levers carry it. The −15% floor lives in the shared Strike line: the fist is 1d6 and there is no flurry. The +30% / +100% lives in the Techniques and the boons, and the sky multiplies it.

For offensive Cloths the multiplier is paid in dice. For defensive, control, and utility Cloths it is paid in scope — bigger auras, more removal, longer range. That is why their flat damage line is correct rather than broken. Only the offensive Cloths move the damage meter, by design.

The floor is a feature

Set this expectation out loud: "You're a Gold Saint every day; the sky tells the world which day is yours." A player who expects to be Aiolia every session wants a Fighter, not a Saint.

Techniques have no rank. You gain four, and each heightens once per 2 character levels above the level it was gained.

SlotGainedFair single-targetFair area
1st (Signature)12d61d8
2nd66d63d8
3rd (Cloth Ability)1112d66d8
4th (Ultimate)1616d68d8

Spines: single-target spell attack +2d6 per step; area basic save +1d8 per step. All four converge on 20d6 / 10d8 by 20th level — early Techniques never become dead weight, and later slots buy new shapes, not bigger numbers.

Spell attacks get no potency runes. A Technique's attack bonus is 2 lower than your Strike. Say this at the table.

The sky heightens you

This is the mechanism the whole class turns on:

  • Ascendant — Techniques heighten as though you were +4 levels (2 extra steps).
  • Zenith — as though +8 levels (4 extra steps).
  • Cloth Attunement (17th) — one further step, always.

How this is implemented in Foundry

PF2e has no rankless spell, so each Technique is a focus spell whose base rank is half its gain level rounded up — 1, 3, 6, 8. Focus spells auto-heighten to half your level rounded up, which reproduces the guide exactly for the 1st and 3rd Techniques and converges correctly at 20th for all four.

The 2nd and 4th slots run one heightening step ahead of the guide between odd levels, because pf2e anchors focus rank to odd levels while the guide anchors to the gain level. The alternative was printing the wrong number at the level the Technique is gained, which is what a player actually reads.

The sky's extra steps are automated as bonus damage dice on each Technique, predicated on the sky:ascendant and sky:zenith roll options. Riders that scale with heightening but aren't damage — extra targets, longer range, wider bursts — are in each Technique's text and applied by hand.

The sky is a world setting, and the module ships a tracker window to drive it: a scene-control button beside the token tools, an entry in module settings, and a Set Today's Sky macro as a fallback if a Foundry update ever breaks the window.

What the tracker does

  • Holds the day's sign (twelve constellations plus Starless) and aspect (Quiet, Benefic, Retrograde, Malefic, Exalted).
  • Applies the right Sky: Ascendant or Sky: Zenith effect to every Saint whose Cloth matches the day, and removes it when the day turns. It only ever touches effects it applied itself, so anything you dragged on by hand is safe.
  • Never applies Malefic or Retrograde riders to a Saint at all. That is @UUID[Compendium.isaacs-hb-pf2e.saint-class-features.Item.Unfailing Cosmo], enforced rather than remembered.
  • Pre-rolls the next seven days, so Read the Constellation has a fixed answer that cannot be re-rolled for a better one.

Schedule your Zeniths

One day in 260 means a Zenith will never happen by chance. Exalted has a roll weight of zero — the only way to one is the tracker's Schedule Zenith button. Write "your sign, Exalted" on the card before the arc climax. That scene is the whole class.

Everything else

Every boon lives in an effect item, and every "on any day your constellation is ascendant" clause keys off the roll option sky:ascendant (with sky:zenith on the Zenith tier). If you build your own equivalent effect and set those options, all the feats still fire.

text.content:

♏ ScorpioOffense, rampScarlet NeedleCrimson MirageCrimson FlurryAntares
♐ SagittariusOffense + utilityGolden ArrowChiron's Light ImpulseInfinity BreakAiolos's Wings
♑ CapricornOffense, conditionalExcaliburJumping StoneDouble ExcaliburThe Sword That Cuts Everything
♒ AquariusOffense + removalDiamond DustKoliçoFreezing ShieldFreezing Coffin
♓ PiscesOffense, auraPiranha RoseRoyal Demon RoseCrimson FogRoyal Funeral

Incapacitation is load-bearing

Never drop the incapacitation trait from the Cancer, Scorpio, Virgo all-senses, Aquarius, or Pisces death and removal effects. Without it they cheese bosses outright. The module's build validates this: those Techniques fail the build if the trait goes missing.

Capricorn needs you to seed a target

Capricorn is a key, not a hammer. Its boon swings from +0% against a boss with no resistances to +170% against resistance 10. On the day Capricorn rises, put something resistant in the encounter — or tell the player up front that this is the design, and that the answer to "what's behind the wall?" is the whole question.

Cosmo Strike replaces handwraps

@UUID[Compendium.isaacs-hb-pf2e.saint-class-features.Item.Cosmo Strike] already grants the magical trait and +1 damage per weapon die. Do not also hand out handwraps of mighty blows — that taxes an unarmed-only class twice.

Two Saints, one Cloth

There is one Gold Cloth per sign. A second claimant is not a character option, it is a campaign.

What this class is measured against

The benchmark is a Monk with focus spells: about 10 damage per round against a boss and 31 against a mob at 11th level. The Saint's job is to beat a Monk, not a Magus — a Magus still solo-clears the mob encounter and that is fine.

Om is a real cost

A blinded Virgo genuinely cannot see. Do not let the table hand-wave it before 7th level, when Sixth Sense makes it survivable — that gap is the mechanic. The Om action applies Effect: Om, which holds the stack count and applies the blinded condition automatically for as long as your eyes are closed. Opening them removes both.

Where the automation stops

Four things are text rather than rules, because PF2e has no hook for them:

  • Blanket "ignore all resistances" (Seventh Sense, Capricorn's boon). Material bypass and incorporeality are automated; the general clause is a roll note on the damage.
  • Scorpio's per-creature needle counts. The sheet resource tracks the current target and the toggles flag the 5 / 10 / 14 thresholds; several creatures at once need pen and paper.
  • Gemini's Zenith duplicate. Copy the token, give it 2 actions of Strike and Stride only, and delete it at the top of the next turn.
  • The non-damage half of a heightening step — extra targets, longer range, wider bursts. The sky's extra dice are automated; the rest is in each Technique's text.
